newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS SIGN DEFENSEMAN DAVE ELLETT.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS SIGN DEFENSEMAN DAVE ELLETT.

text.p: The Boston Bruins signed unrestricted free-agent defenceman Dave Ellett to a three-year contract Wednesday, hoping to improve the National Hockey League's weakest defence.

The 33-year-old Ellett split the 1996-97 season between the Toronto Maple Leafs and New Jersey Devils, combining for six goals and 15 assists in 76 games. He was acquired by New Jersey in a five-player trade on February 25.
The 13-year veteran broke in with the Winnipeg Jets in 1984-85 and spent six-plus seasons with them until he was dealt to Toronto in a four-play trade in November 1990.

Ellett has never spent a day in the minor leagues and has had three 50-point seasons. His offensive production has dropped markedly in recent years, and he has cracked the 20-point mark just once since 1994.

"In assessing our needs for the upcoming season, we wanted to add an experienced defenceman who was capable at both ends of the ice," said assistant general manager Mike O'Connell. "Dave fits that description very well and, additionally, he brings leadership qualities that can only benefit our younger players."
The Bruins in 1996-97 allowed 300 goals, 20 more than any other team.
